name: litehtml0.9
reason: Real library — "Fast and lightweight HTML/CSS rendering engine", embedded in other apps, not launchable on its own. No safe general pattern (versioned-library names like this collide with real apps that also carry a bare version number, e.g. 0ad/7zip/openttd).

name: cs-signal
reason: Real library — "Library for thread aware signal/slot delivery" (CopperSpice's signal/slot mechanism). No safe general pattern: re-checked the whole real cs-* family on a later pass looking for one — cs-bin ("codespelunker", a real CLI code-search tool), cs-prolog (a real standalone Prolog interpreter), and cs-script (a real standalone C# script runner) are all real, unrelated tools that just happen to share the CopperSpice prefix coincidentally, confirming a "cs-" pattern would be unsafe.

name: claude-cowork-rs
reason: Real support package — "Linux daemon for Claude Desktop Cowork (Local Agent Mode)", a background helper process for a different app (Claude Desktop), not launchable on its own. No name-pattern would catch this (the word "daemon" is only in the description, not the name).

name: biosig4c++
reason: Real library — "A software library for processing of biomedical signals", hasDesktopFile:false. No safe general pattern: a bare "c++" substring check has real counter-examples (Gentoo's c++robots, a real King-of-the-Hill programming game).

name: adblock
reason: Same real library as filter/rules.ts's python-adblock pattern (Brave's adblock-parsing engine), but Gentoo's dev-python naming convention doesn't carry the python-prefix that pattern matches on — bare "adblock" isn't safe to generalize (Gentoo's dev-python category itself isn't safe to exclude wholesale either — verified live it mixes in real CLI tools: black, bpython, ipython, poetry).
